subject: Staged swap fallback matrix & validation windows
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Tanya Shah <tanya@bluehelix.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Staged swap fallback matrix & validation windows

Hi Tanya —

Thanks again for committing to Dedicated for BlueHelix (excited to get you off the shared pool). Attached is an initial staged-swap plan and fallback matrix I mentioned on the call (staged_swap_matrix_v1.xlsx). High level proposal below: 

- Canary window (small % traffic, 2 hours): validate model parity and latency SLOs under representative user mix.
- Staged ramp (Day 1–3): increase traffic in 4 steps, 12–24 hour hold at each step for telemetry review.
- Full cutover (Day 4): final routing flip with 6-hour monitored blackout and rapid rollback plan.
- Fallbacks: auto-failover to hosted variant + regional fallback if sustained errors or token-level QoQ regressions.

Acceptance criteria we want to validate in the canary:
1) 95th p95 latency within 15% of hosted baseline for the most common prompt archetypes.
2) Token-level rate of hallucination/regression on our eval set below 2% (as measured by the sanity prompts).
3) No more than 10% estimated cost delta versus committed expectations once batching and KV cache are enabled.

Could you confirm the preferred maintenance window for the canary and whether you want us to mirror 100% of a single region or a user-segment mirror? If you prefer, we can propose exact timestamps for UTC and PST windows.

Next steps: if you sign off, we’ll schedule a dry-run rehearsal with the infra team and legal (we’ll attach the commit SLA draft in the follow-up).

Thanks —
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks | Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Tanya Shah <tanya@bluehelix.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueHelix Legal <contracts@bluehelix.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged swap fallback matrix & validation windows

Dylan —

Thanks for the plan and the attachment. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Preferred maintenance window: weekdays 02:00–06:00 UTC (low traffic). Can we run the canary inside that window?
- Mirror approach: we’d prefer a user-segment mirror (10% of active customers in the EU/US segments) rather than full regional mirror. That keeps risk lower.
- Peak QPS: during our morning spike we hit ~18 qps sustained for 10 minutes; can you confirm the expected headroom for the canary given batching/quantization?

Also our legal team flagged the SLA draft line around data retention and audit logs — they’ll need that clarified before we go live. I’ve cc'd contracts@bluehelix.ai.

Happy to run the dry-run on Dec 3 if that works for you.

Best,
Tanya

Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Staged swap fallback matrix & validation windows

Hi Tanya —

Thanks for the quick reply — we can absolutely run the canary in the 02:00–06:00 UTC window. Quick answers to your questions and some numbers you can hand to your SREs: 

- Peak headroom for canary: for the proposed 10% user-segment mirror (target ~= 9 qps sustained, spikes to 12 qps), we recommend a 1.5x safety buffer on the committed GPU profile. That means provisioning equivalent of 1.5x the model’s steady-state footprint to handle bursts during the canary.
- Batching/quantization plan: we’ll enable continuous batching and 4-bit quantization profile in canary mode — expected cost delta: +6–9% initially, with expected convergence to +2–4% after KV caching warms over 24–48 hours. Details are in the kvcache-estimates.csv attachment.
- Acceptance hooks: we’ll instrument the eval prompts (attached) and run a daily regression job during the staged ramp. If token-level regressions exceed 2% for two consecutive checks, we trigger manual rollback.

On contract/SLA items: I attached commit-sla-draft.docx with a redline for audit log retention and a clause for a one-time credit if the swap exceeds the agreed rollback window due to infra regressions. Legal can review and I’ll loop Monica from our contracts team to accelerate.

Proposed rehearsal timeline:
- Dec 3, 02:00–03:00 UTC — Dry-run canary (no live traffic; smoke validation).
- Dec 4, 02:00–06:00 UTC — Live 2-hour canary + 2-hour hold for telemetry.
- Dec 5–7 — Staged ramp with daily regression reviews.

If that looks good I’ll open the infra ticket and attach the stress-run logs from a previous rehearsal (for your SREs to baseline).

Cheers,
Marissa
